assumptions.condition: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(M^s\) is a recursive finite-state SCM compatible with \(G\) on \(\mathcal X\).
In every domain \(s\), the exogenous response blocks associated with distinct elements of \(\mathcal D(G)\) are mutually independent.
For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\) with \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), the joint law of the structural response maps on \(D\) in \(M^s\) equals its law in \(M^\star\).

novel.justification: A shared laboratory pipeline, record-linkage platform, or policy module can preserve the entire latent response block for a confounded district across sites. This is deliberately stronger than ordinary vertex-level selection-diagram invariance because Layer-3 laws depend on cross-world coupling inside the district.

assumptions.condition: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), either \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).

novel.justification: Site changes often act on an entire confounded measurement or policy block. Whole-district selection permits arbitrary changes inside that block while ruling out an unsupported splice of cross-world dependence across only part of it.

assumptions.condition: For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), \(P_a^s\) equals the law induced by regime \(a\) in \(M^s\).
For every \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), the bidirected subgraph induced by \(D\) is complete.

For every \(s\in\mathcal S\) and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), all mechanisms on \(D\) are generated by one finite latent variable \(U_D^s\in\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\), where \(\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\) contains the deterministic response maps at every parent configuration: if \(U_D^s=\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\), then the structural equation of each \(V\in D\) reads the component \(f_V\); the variables \((U_D^s:D\in\mathcal D(G))\) are mutually independent.

definitions.name: District-closed finite transport class
definitions.construction: \[\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})=\{\mathbf M=(M^s:s\in\mathcal S):\mathbf M\text{ is recursively compatible, district-factorized, district-kernel invariant, and district-closed}\}.\]

definitions.name: Typed-menu compatibility fiber
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):P_{M^s}^{a}=P_a^s\text{ for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s\}.\]

definitions.name: Canonical district response profile
definitions.construction: For each \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), enumerate every tuple of deterministic maps \(\omega_D=(f_V:V\in D)\) on the parent configurations visited by \(B_\rho\), \(E\), and \(\mathcal P\); the resulting finite set is \(\Omega_D\), and \(q_D^s(\omega_D)=P_{M^s}(\omega_D)\).

definitions.name: Certified typed extraction judgment
definitions.construction: For \(P_a^s\in\Delta(\mathcal X_{W_a})\), write \[\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\] exactly when consistency, unnesting, ancestor restriction, fixing, and marginalization define a kernel \(K_{s,a,D}:H_{s,a,D}\to\Delta(C_{s,a,D})\) and \(\kappa\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) certifies every context, marginal, and nonzero divisor used. An undefined fixing, unavailable context, or uncertified quotient has no successful judgment.

definitions.name: Context-indexed extracted-cell incidence row
definitions.construction: \[r_{s,a,D,h,c}(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{\omega_D\text{ produces extracted cell }c\text{ at context }h\text{ under regime }a\},\qquad\omega_D\in\Omega_D.\]

definitions.name: Source-labelled lossless stacked district system
definitions.construction:
For each complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\), first prove the transport-admissibility predicate \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  If recursive evaluation of \(C_{a,v}\) visits only \(D\), retain before all derived rows the raw identity-extraction row
\[
r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{C_{a,v}\text{ is true under }\omega_D\},
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D,
\]
with value \(P_a^s(v)\).  Thus every transport-admissible complete-menu cell whose reduction is district-local is retained even when no nontrivial fixing quotient is available.  Next, for every successful judgment \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\) with the same admissibility proof, retain every available row \(r_{s,a,D,h,c}\) and value \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)\).  Prepend \(\mathbf 1^\top\), stack the normalization row, raw rows, and derived rows in canonical order as \(A_D\), and stack their values as \(m_D\).  A failed derived extraction creates no derived row, but it does not delete an independently certified raw district-local row.  A changed-district source cell and a cell whose recursive indicator depends on more than \(D\) create no row in \(A_D\); their complete equalities remain in the global response-profile or graph-compatible canonical fiber.

definitions.name: District row face and global projections
definitions.construction:
Define the district row face and its forced-zero coordinates by
\[
\mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{\Omega_D}:A_Dq=m_D\},
\qquad
Z_D(m_D)=\{\omega\in\Omega_D:q(\omega)=0\text{ for every }q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\}.
\]
Define the broad and saturated global district projections by
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\},
\qquad
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]

definitions.name: Common-evidence arm row system
definitions.construction: Reduce \(B_\rho\cap E\) and \(E\) to target-district cells and evaluate them on \(\Omega_D\), obtaining \(n_{\rho,D}\) and \(d_D\); set \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}\). The same reduction applied to any target cell gives \(b_D\).

definitions.name: Sharp transported dominance margin
definitions.construction: \[\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=\min_{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q,\qquad \overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=\max_{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q.\]

definitions.name: Menu-dual dominance certificate
definitions.construction: A certificate at level \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\) is a vector \(\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) satisfying \(A_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\) coordinatewise and \(m_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\ge\gamma\).

definitions.name: One-cell Layer-3 sign-regime frontier
definitions.construction: \[I_D=\{r_D^\dagger q:q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\},\qquad\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)=\min_{\substack{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\\ r_D^\dagger q=p}}g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q,\qquad\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+=\{p\in I_D:\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)>0\}.\]

definitions.name: Finite ex-post regime-block acquisition problem
definitions.construction: For each realizable experiment \(e\in\mathcal U\), the dependent block \((R_e,p_e)\) is revealed jointly at cost \(c_e>0\). For \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\), define \[\mathcal K_S=\{q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D):R_eq=p_e\text{ for every }e\in S\},\qquad \operatorname{PO}(S)=\{\rho:\exists q\in\mathcal K_S,\ \forall\sigma\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}},\ Q_\rho(q)\ge Q_\sigma(q)\},\] \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{PO}(\mathcal U),\qquad \min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e\quad\text{subject to}\quad\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}},\qquad f(S)=\lvert\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\rvert-\lvert\operatorname{PO}(S)\rvert.\]

definitions.name: Complete binary acquisition and strictness instance
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\) have binary \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\to Y\) and isolated binary \(Z\), target \(\star\), source \(s\), and \(\Delta_s=\{Z\}\), so the invariant district is \(D=\{Y\}\). Set \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\), \(E=\top\), \(B_\rho=\{(Y_0,Y_1):Y_0\ne Y_1\}\), \(B_\sigma=\{(Y_0,Y_1):Y_1=1\}\), and \(\mathcal U=\{e^\dagger\}\). Order \(\Omega_D=\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}\) for \((Y_0,Y_1)\), and set \[A_D=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&1&1\\0&0&1&1\\0&1&0&1\end{bmatrix},\quad m_D=(1,1/2,1/2)^\top,\quad \mathcal K_D(m_D)=\{q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p):0\le p\le1/2\},\quad Z_D(m_D)=\varnothing.\] The event incidence rows are \(n_{\rho,D}=(0,1,1,0)\), \(n_{\sigma,D}=(0,1,0,1)\), and \(d_D=(1,1,1,1)\), so \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=(0,0,-1,1)\). The sole block has \(c_{e^\dagger}=1\), \(R_{e^\dagger}=r_D^\dagger=(0,0,0,1)\), and reveals the genuine Layer-3 source cell \(p_{e^\dagger}=p=P^s(Y_0=1,Y_1=1)=3/8\). Also set \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\).

definitions.name: Allowed rational functional
definitions.construction: \(\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\) is the typed expression-and-certificate algebra generated from menu cells by finite sums, differences, products, marginalization sums, and quotients carrying a proof that the divisor is nonzero on the relevant compatibility fiber.

definitions.name: DCTFTR syntax, configurations, and terminals
definitions.construction:
Fix canonical finite orders on vertices, regimes, districts, assignments, and generated DAG-node identifiers. The event grammar is \[\mathsf{Atom}::=[s]\,V_{\alpha}=v,\qquad \mathsf{Event}::=	op\mid ot\mid\mathsf{Atom}\mid\mathsf{Event}\wedge\mathsf{Event}\mid\mathsf{Event}\vee\mathsf{Event},\] where \(\alpha\) is a finite well-typed intervention or partial-copy term and canonical normalized events are disjoint normal forms of unnested atoms. Identified expressions have grammar \[\mathsf{Expr}::=\operatorname{Cell}(s,a,u)\mid\operatorname{Rat}(r)\mid\sum_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j\mid\prod_{j\in J}\mathsf{Expr}_j\mid\operatorname{Quot}(F,G,
u_G),\] where \(r\in\mathbb Q\) and \(
u_G\) is an independently checked nonzero certificate. The phase-indexed node grammar is exactly \[\mathsf{Goal}::=\operatorname{Raw}(	au,e)\mid\operatorname{Normed}(	au,e,
u)\mid\operatorname{AncClosed}(	au,H,e,\alpha)\mid\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\mid\operatorname{NeedFace}(	au,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)\mid\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})\mid\operatorname{Prod}(\mathrm{children})\mid\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta),\] with \(	au\in\{\mathrm{num},\mathrm{den}\}\). A configuration is a finite well-typed acyclic work DAG of these nodes, its numerator and denominator roots, and a checked trace. For every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), node denotation is defined recursively: the first three event phases denote their target event probability; \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\) and \(\operatorname{NeedFace}(	au,D,b,A,m,Z,\kappa)\) denote \(bq_D^\star(\mathbf M)\); \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F,\delta)\) denotes \(F(\mathcal P)\); and sum and product nodes denote the corresponding finite sum and product of child denotations. Configuration denotation is the ordered pair of root values. Checked derivations are finite syntax trees: normalization derivations use only consistency, unnesting, contradiction, Boolean normalization, and finite disjoint-additivity constructors; ancestor derivations enumerate summed assignments; district-split derivations enumerate the districts of \(G[H]\) and use finite marginalization and semi-Markovian district factorization; extraction derivations record each fixing, marginalization, context lookup, and certified quotient; face certificates are exact rational LP or Farkas certificates; and zero, nonzero, or strict-positivity certificates are checked by exact rational ring normalization together with Farkas certificates for linear face constraints or displayed sum-of-squares preordering identities for the finite response-law constraints. Thus no certificate constructor consists merely of the semantic equality or inequality being certified. The terminals are \[\mathsf{Result}::=\operatorname{ID}(F,\delta)\mid\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\mid\operatorname{FAIL}(t),\] where a conditioning derivation \(\delta\) records the numerator derivation, denominator derivation, and positivity certificate. Failure constructors include \(\operatorname{SPLIT\_UNDEFINED}(v,\mathrm{reason},t)\), \(\operatorname{EXTRACTION\_UNDEFINED}(s,a,D,h)\), \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}(D,b,A,m,Z,w_{\mathrm{local}},t)\), \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}(D,b,\mathrm{retainedRows},t)\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}(E,\mathbf M,t)\), \(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}(E,t)\), and \(\operatorname{STUCK}(\mathrm{phase},\mathrm{reason},t)\).

definitions.name: District-closed Layer-3 transport recursion
definitions.construction:
Initialize one finite acyclic work DAG with roots \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{num},B_ho\wedge E)\) and \(\operatorname{Raw}(\mathrm{den},E)\); its denotation at \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) is \((P_{M^\star}(B_ho\wedge E),P_{M^\star}(E))\). The deterministic transition system \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) has these eight rules. \(\mathsf{NORM}\): replace the least \(\operatorname{Raw}(	au,e)\) by \(\operatorname{Normed}(	au,\operatorname{nf}(e),
u)\), where the total finite-state checker applies consistency, unnesting, contradiction removal, and disjoint-normal-form rewriting and returns a derivation \(
u:P(e)=P(\operatorname{nf}(e))\); append \(\operatorname{NORM}(v,e,\operatorname{nf}(e),
u)\). \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\): for the least normalized node, enumerate its counterfactual ancestors \(H\), the assignments summed out, and a checked finite marginalization derivation \(\alpha\), then replace it by \(\operatorname{AncClosed}(	au,H,e|_H,\alpha)\) and append \(\operatorname{ANCESTOR}(v,H,\alpha)\). \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\): for the least ancestor-closed node, the compiler mechanically enumerates \(G[H]\), its districts, and all finite summation assignments and builds an acyclic sum-product DAG with leaves \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\); its checker constructs \(\sigma\) from finite marginalization and district-factorization rules, the DAG is spliced in, and \(\operatorname{SPLIT}(v,D_1,\ldots,D_k,\sigma)\) is appended. If enumeration or typing is undefined, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{SPLIT\_UNDEFINED}(v,\mathrm{reason},t))\). \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\): at the least \(\operatorname{NeedRows}(	au,D,b)\), enumerate all supplied \((s,a)\) and their complete cells canonically.  After a checked proof of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), first retain every complete cell whose recursive indicator visits only \(D\) as the raw equality \(P_a^s(v)=r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}q_D^\star\).  Then retain a derived context and cell only when \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\) succeeds with the same admissibility proof; the recomputed extraction tree must prove \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^\star\). Record every failed derived extraction, changed-district rejection, and cross-district raw cell without turning it into a district row. Prepend the normalization row, stack accepted raw and derived rows and values canonically as \((A_D,m_D)\), even if no non-normalization row survives, replace the node by \(\operatorname{NeedFace}(	au,D,b,A_D,m_D,Z_D(m_D),\kappa_{\mathrm{all}})\), and append the accepted rows, rejected candidates, admissibility proofs, and derivations; \(\kappa_{\mathrm{all}}\) checks \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\). \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\): for the least face node, compute \(Z=\{\omega:q(\omega)=0	ext{ for every }q\ge0	ext{ with }Aq=m\}\), with an exact LP or Farkas certificate for every coordinate, and test \(b\in\operatorname{row}(A)+\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z\}\). If membership holds, fixed-pivot reduced row echelon form chooses \(b=\lambda^	op A+\sum_{\omega\in Z}\zeta_\omega e_\omega\); replace the node by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\lambda^	op m,\delta_{\mathrm{face}})\), where the checker verifies \(bq=\lambda^	op Aq+\sum_{\omega\in Z}\zeta_\omega q(\omega)=\lambda^	op m\), and append the certificates. If membership fails, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}(D,b,A,m,Z,w_{\mathrm{local}},t))\); \(w_{\mathrm{local}}\) witnesses only variation in the district row relaxation.  It is not a pair of globally compatible SCMs unless district saturation and the district-separated one-district projection hypotheses have been checked. If no non-normalization raw or derived row succeeded, use \(\operatorname{NO\_ADMISSIBLE\_FACTOR}\) instead only after this normalization-only face test fails. \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\): replace the least ready \(\operatorname{Sum}(J,\mathrm{children})\), all of whose children are resolved, by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\sum_{j\in J}F_j,\delta_{\mathrm{sum}})\), using finite additivity and child derivations. \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\): replace the least ready product node by \(\operatorname{Resolved}(\prod_jF_j,\delta_{\mathrm{prod}})\), using district factorization and child derivations. \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\): when both roots are \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F_B,\delta_B)\) and \(\operatorname{Resolved}(F_E,\delta_E)\), append a condition record and return \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\) if the independent zero calculus proves \(F_E=0\) throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\); return \(\operatorname{ID}(\operatorname{Quot}(F_B,F_E,\pi),\delta_B,\delta_E,\pi)\) if the independent positivity calculus proves \(F_E>0\) throughout that fiber; return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_MAY\_VANISH}(E,\mathbf M,t))\) if an explicitly checked \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) has \(F_E=0\); otherwise return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{DENOMINATOR\_POSITIVITY\_UNCERTIFIED}(E,t))\). Rule priority is \(\mathsf{NORM}>\mathsf{ANCESTOR}>\mathsf{SPLIT}>\mathsf{EXTRACT}>\mathsf{FACE\_ID}>\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}>\mathsf{PRODUCT}>\mathsf{CONDITION}\); within a rule choose the least applicable node, where applicability includes readiness. No rule creates an earlier-phase node. For nonterminals, \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi},r_C)\): the rules respectively decrease the indicated first still-changeable coordinate, with \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) changing \(r_C=1\) to zero after the first seven coordinates vanish; later coordinates may increase. If no rule applies to a nonterminal, return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\operatorname{STUCK}(\mathrm{phase},\mathrm{reason},t))\).

definitions.name: Cross-menu face-preservation handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{preserve}}\) starts from the exact feasible face \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) and tracks both its affine hull and forced-zero coordinates through ancestor restriction, fixing, district splitting, and marginalization in \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\).

definitions.name: Layer-3 menu-acquisition handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{acquire}}\) enumerates realizable regime blocks \((R_e,p_e)\), propagates each full dependent block through the finite dual bases defining arm values on \(\mathcal K_S\), and solves the finite ex-post covering problem \(\min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U}\sum_{e\in S}c_e\) subject to \(\operatorname{PO}(S)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).

definitions.name: Partial-district invariance-frontier handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{leak}}\) splits a selected district response kernel across \(D\cap\Delta_s\) and \(D\setminus\Delta_s\), tests whether supplied and target Layer-3 factors depend on a common invariant marginal kernel, and searches the smallest binary crossing perturbation when they do not.

definitions.name: Exact saturated response-profile and sparse canonical fibers
definitions.construction:
For a response-profile tuple \(\theta=(q_D^s:s\in\mathcal S,\ D\in\mathcal D(G))\) with \(q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)\), define, for every finite counterfactual cell \(C\),
\[
\Psi_C^s(\theta^s)=
\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1\{C\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }\omega\}
\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^s(\omega_D).
\]
If the recursive indicator of \(C\) depends on the profiles in \(k\) districts, then \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district probability blocks and has total degree at most \(k\).  Writing \(C_{a,v}\) for the complete cell in which descriptor \(a\) returns \(v\in\mathcal X_{W_a}\), define the saturated response-profile fiber
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\theta:{}&q_D^s\in\Delta(\Omega_D)
\quad(s\in\mathcal S,\ D\in\mathcal D(G)),\\
&q_D^s=q_D^\star\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Psi_{C_{a,v}}^s(\theta^s)=P_a^s(v)
\quad\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S,\ a\in\mathcal A_s,
\ v\in\mathcal X_{W_a}\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
For a target cell \(T\), set
\[
L_T(\mathcal P)=\min_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\qquad
U_T(\mathcal P)=\max_{\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)}\Psi_T^\star(\theta^\star),
\]
and define
\[
\mathcal G_{\rho,\sigma}(\theta)
=\Psi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star)
-\Psi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(\theta^\star).
\]

For an arbitrary, possibly nonsaturated ADMG \(G\), retain a separate graph-compatible canonical parameter \(\vartheta^s=(\mu^s,p^s)\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\).  Its simplex and one-hot coordinates satisfy
\[
p_U^s(u)\geq0,\qquad \sum_up_U^s(u)=1,
\qquad \mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s\in\{0,1\},
\qquad \sum_{v\in\mathcal X_V}\mu_{V,v\mid pa,u_V}^s=1,
\]
with the graph-compatible latent-factor restrictions and product law across distinct districts retained.  Let \(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)\) be the finite recursive canonical cell polynomial and let \(q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)\) be its induced joint response-profile law on \(D\).  Define
\[
\begin{split}
\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)=\bigl\{\vartheta:{}&
\vartheta^s\in\operatorname{Can}(G,\mathcal X)\quad(s\in\mathcal S),\\
&q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\cdot;\vartheta^s)=q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\cdot;\vartheta^\star)
\quad\text{if }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing,\\
&\Phi_{C_{a,v},\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)=P_a^s(v)
\quad\text{for every complete supplied cell}\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The first fiber deliberately uses district-saturated response-block semantics; the second retains all internal latent-factor restrictions of a sparse \(G\).

definitions.name: Saturated typed-menu compatibility fiber
definitions.construction:
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\cap\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat}}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}).
\]

definitions.name: District-separated complete-menu condition
definitions.construction: For \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), the predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds when every complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in a domain satisfying \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) has, under recursive evaluation on \(\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_{D'}\), an indicator that is either independent of \(\omega_D\), or depends only on \(\omega_D\).  In the second case its raw row \(r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}\) and value \(P_a^s(v)\) must occur in \((A_D,m_D)\).  This is a finite syntactic and tabular condition; it excludes an unrecorded cross-district polynomial constraint involving \(q_D^\star\).

definitions.name: District-saturated response-block transport subclass
definitions.construction:
Define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat}}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
=\bigl\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):{}&
G[D]\text{ is bidirected complete for every }D\in\mathcal D(G);\\
&\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S\text{ and }D\in\mathcal D(G),
\text{ exactly one finite latent block }U_D^s\text{ taking values in }\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\\
&\text{stores one full deterministic response map for every vertex in }D
\text{ at every parent configuration};\\
&\text{each structural equation in }D\text{ reads the corresponding component of }U_D^s;\\
&(U_D^s:D\in\mathcal D(G))\text{ are mutually independent within each domain }s;\\
&\text{the class contains every independent choice of one probability law on }
\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\text{ for each permitted district block},\\
&\text{subject only to equality of the laws of }U_D^s\text{ and }U_D^\star
\text{ whenever }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
Thus changed districts may use arbitrary and mutually unrelated response-block laws, unchanged districts use exactly the target response-block law, and no equality with the broad sparse-ADMG class \(\mathfrak M\) is asserted.

definitions.name: Focal-district-saturated response-block transport subclass and fiber
definitions.construction:
For a fixed district \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
=\bigl\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}):{}&
G[D]\text{ is bidirected complete};\\
&\text{for every }s\in\mathcal S\text{ there is exactly one finite latent block }
U_D^s\in\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\\
&\text{storing one full deterministic response map for each vertex in }D
\text{ at every allowed parent configuration};\\
&\text{each structural equation of a vertex in }D
\text{ reads the corresponding component of }U_D^s;\\
&U_D^s\text{ is independent of the exogenous blocks of every }D'\ne D;\\
&\text{every probability law on }\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\text{ is permitted for }U_D^s,
\text{ subject only to equality with the target law}\\
&\text{when }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing;\\
&\text{for each }D'\ne D\text{, all structural tables, latent-factor restrictions,}
\text{ and cross-domain equalities remain those of }\mathfrak M
\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The phrase ``every probability law is permitted'' includes closure under replacing the law of \(U_D^\star\) and all its unchanged-source copies while holding all mechanisms and latent laws in districts \(D'\ne D\), and all changed-source copies of \(U_D\), fixed. Define
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\cap
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat},D}(G,\mathcal X,\mathcal S,\{\Delta_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S})
\]
and
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)
=\{q_D^\star(\mathbf M):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]

definitions.name: Active-slice face-separation condition
definitions.construction:
For a fixed district \(D\), define its active row space by
\[
R_D(m_D)=\operatorname{row}(A_D)+
\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\}
\subseteq\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}.
\]
For a complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\) that is transport-admissible for \(D\), meaning \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), and for
\(\omega_{-D}\in\prod_{D'\in\mathcal D(G),\,D'\ne D}\Omega_{D'}\), define its focal recursive-indicator slice by
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}(\omega_D)
=\mathbf 1\{C_{a,v}\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }
(\omega_D,\omega_{-D})\},
\qquad \omega_D\in\Omega_D.
\]
The active-slice face-separation predicate \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds exactly when
\[
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}\in R_D(m_D)
\]
for every transport-admissible complete supplied cell and every fixed nonfocal response profile \(\omega_{-D}\).  When \(D\) is the only district, the nonfocal product is the singleton empty profile.

statements.statement: If \(\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa)\), then for every available \(h\in H_{s,a,D}\) and \(c\in C_{s,a,D}\), \[K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^s.\] After, and only after, proving \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), district-kernel invariance gives \(K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^\star\). The target arm numerator, evidence, and generic target cells equal \(n_{\rho,D}q_D^\star\), \(d_Dq_D^\star\), and \(b_Dq_D^\star\), respectively. Failed extraction yields no incidence row.
statements.justification: This converts every heterogeneous Layer-3 input and each target arm comparison into exact linear information on a fixed response carrier.
statements.gap: Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim give canonical response carriers, while CTFIDU+ extracts Layer-3 factors; neither gives a source-labelled common-evidence row system under district-level transport.
statements.consumer: The row representation supplies the primal and dual programs used by the face-aware identification and arm-ordering certificates.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(s\in\mathcal S\), \(a\in\mathcal A_s\), and \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\), and suppose
\[
\operatorname{Extract}_{s,a,D}(P_a^s)\Downarrow(K_{s,a,D},\kappa).
\]
For \(h\in H_{s,a,D}\) and \(c\in C_{s,a,D}\), let
\[
S(h,c)=\{\omega_D\in\Omega_D:\omega_D\text{ produces }c
\text{ at context }h\text{ under }a\}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:incidence\text{-}row}\),
\[
r_{s,a,D,h,c}(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{\omega_D\in S(h,c)\}.
\]
The successful judgment in \(\mathrm{def:typed\text{-}extraction\text{-}judgment}\) certifies every consistency, unnesting, fixing, marginalization, context lookup, and nonzero quotient used to form \(K_{s,a,D}\). By \(\mathrm{ass:typed\text{-}menu\text{-}realizability}\), the supplied law is the regime law of \(M^s\); by \(\mathrm{ass:recursive\text{-}compatibility}\), the extracted cell is deterministic conditional on \(\omega_D\). Finite total probability therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)
&=\sum_{\omega_D\in\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1\{\omega_D\in S(h,c)\}q_D^s(\omega_D)\\
&=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^s.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every quotient used here is legal because its nonzero premise occurs in \(\kappa\).

If \(s=\star\), then \(q_D^s=q_D^\star\) by notation. If \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}kernel\text{-}invariance}\) gives equality of the joint structural-response laws on \(D\), hence again \(q_D^s=q_D^\star\). Only after one of these two admissibility facts is established may one conclude
\[
K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^\star.
\]

Finally, \(\mathrm{def:target\text{-}arm\text{-}rows}\) evaluates the deterministic indicators of \(B_\rho\cap E\), \(E\), and a generic district-local target cell on \(\Omega_D\). Thus
\[
P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\cap E)=n_{\rho,D}q_D^\star,
\qquad
P_{M^\star}(E)=d_Dq_D^\star,
\qquad
P_{M^\star}(\text{target cell})=b_Dq_D^\star.
\]
By the extraction and stacking definitions, a failed judgment has neither a certified kernel cell nor a certified incidence equality and contributes no derived row.

statements.statement:
For every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
Suppose \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds. Then
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
In particular, every boundary point of the row face is induced on the declared alphabets \(\mathcal X\) by a compatible SCM family that is saturated only at the queried district \(D\); all districts \(D'\ne D\) retain their original graph-compatible latent-factor restrictions. The older structural predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) is an easy sufficient test for \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\). Without focal-district saturation or active-slice separation, only the displayed broad inclusion is asserted.
statements.justification: The equality is the causal realization step making focal-district optimization sharp on the original observed alphabets whenever all complete-menu focal slices are already controlled by the active face.
statements.gap: CTFIDU+ proves one-domain completeness by ctf-thickets and may enlarge observed alphabets; it does not give a heterogeneous source-labelled fixed-alphabet projection theorem that preserves cross-district menu cells slice by slice.
statements.consumer: Every local primal optimizer or sign-reversing point becomes an explicit compatible SCM while all nonfocal districts retain their original graph-compatible restrictions.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(D\in\mathcal D(G)\).  Let \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) and put \(q=q_D^\star(\mathbf M)\).  By \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}response\text{-}profile}\), \(q\geq0\) and \(\mathbf 1^\top q=1\).  Consider a raw row retained in \(A_D\).  By \(\mathrm{def:stacked\text{-}menu\text{-}system}\), its retention includes proofs that its supplied complete cell is district-local and that \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\).  Recursive evaluation and \(\mathrm{ass:typed\text{-}menu\text{-}realizability}\) give
\[
P_a^s(v)=r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}q_D^s.
\]
If \(s=\star\), then \(q_D^s=q\) by definition; if \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), then \(q_D^s=q\) by \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}kernel\text{-}invariance}\).  Thus every retained raw equality holds at \(q\).  For a retained derived row, \(\mathrm{lem:district\text{-}cell\text{-}linearity}\), together with the same admissibility proof, gives
\[
K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q.
\]
Stacking normalization, raw, and derived equalities in the order specified by \(\mathrm{def:stacked\text{-}menu\text{-}system}\) yields \(A_Dq=m_D\).  Hence
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]

Now assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\).  The preceding inclusion and \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) imply
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
For the reverse inclusion, choose a baseline \(\mathbf M^0\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\), write \(q_0=q_D^\star(\mathbf M^0)\), and fix arbitrary \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\).  The broad inclusion already proved gives \(q_0\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\), and therefore
\[
A_D(q-q_0)=0,
\qquad
(q-q_0)(\omega)=0\quad\text{for every }\omega\in Z_D(m_D).
\]
Consequently, from the definition of \(R_D(m_D)\),
\[
h(q-q_0)=0\qquad\text{for every }h\in R_D(m_D).
\tag{1}
\]

Every alphabet in \(\mathcal X\) is finite and nonempty.  Complete each partial profile \(\omega_D\in\Omega_D\) at every unvisited parent configuration by a fixed element of the appropriate alphabet, and denote the resulting injection by
\[
\iota_D:\Omega_D\longrightarrow\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}.
\]
In the target domain replace the law of \(U_D^\star\) by \((\iota_D)_\#q\).  Make the identical replacement in every source satisfying \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), retain the baseline law of \(U_D^s\) in every source satisfying \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\), and hold fixed every structural table and latent law in every district \(D'\ne D\).  These two source cases exhaust all possibilities by \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}closure}\).  Call the resulting family \(\mathbf M^q\).

The component-reading structural equations at \(D\) are unchanged, so acyclicity of \(G\) preserves recursive evaluation and every output remains in \(\mathcal X\).  The restrictions at every \(D'\ne D\) are literally those of \(\mathbf M^0\).  Taking the new \(D\)-block marginal independently of the unchanged nonfocal blocks preserves \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\).  The bidirected completeness, full-block representation, and unrestricted-law clause of \(\mathrm{def:focal\text{-}district\text{-}saturated\text{-}model\text{-}class}\) admit \((\iota_D)_\#q\) on the same graph and alphabets.  Equality between the target replacement and each unchanged-source replacement gives \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}kernel\text{-}invariance}\) at \(D\); every other required equality remains true because its blocks were held fixed.  Thus \(\mathbf M^q\) belongs to the focal-district-saturated model class before checking the menu.

Fix a complete supplied cell \(C_{a,v}\) in domain \(s\).  Suppose first that it is transport-admissible for \(D\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\), the baseline law of the nonfocal profile is a product probability law; denote it by \(\nu^s\).  It is unchanged in \(\mathbf M^q\).  Finite total probability and the definition of the focal slice give the exact difference
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{M^{q,s}}^a(v)-P_{M^{0,s}}^a(v)
&=\sum_{\omega_{-D}}
\nu^s(\omega_{-D})
\sum_{\omega_D}
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}(\omega_D)
\{q(\omega_D)-q_0(\omega_D)\}\\
&=\sum_{\omega_{-D}}
\nu^s(\omega_{-D})
\chi_{C_{a,v},\omega_{-D}}(q-q_0).
\end{aligned}
\]
Active-slice separation places every slice in \(R_D(m_D)\), so every summand is zero by (1).  Therefore this supplied cell retains its baseline probability \(P_a^s(v)\).

If the cell is not transport-admissible for \(D\), then \(s\ne\star\) and \(D\cap\Delta_s\ne\varnothing\).  District closure gives \(D\subseteq\Delta_s\), so the \(D\)-block and every nonfocal block in that source were all left at their baseline laws.  Its cell probability is again unchanged.  Thus every complete cell, and hence every supplied law, equals \(\mathcal P\).  We have shown
\[
\mathbf M^q\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P),
\qquad q_D^\star(\mathbf M^q)=q.
\]
This proves the reverse inclusion.  The construction uses only \(q\geq0\) and \(A_Dq=m_D\); it therefore realizes boundary points, preserves the original alphabets, and leaves every \(D'\ne D\) at its graph-compatible baseline.  Finally, \(\mathrm{lem:structural\text{-}separation\text{-}implies\text{-}active\text{-}slice}\) shows that \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) remains a sufficient, though not necessary, check for the new hypothesis.

statements.statement:
For the broad compatibility fiber, membership in the active row space,
\[
b_D\in R_D(m_D)
=\operatorname{row}(A_D)+\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\},
\]
is sufficient for the district-local target \(b_Dq_D^\star\) to be identified, with value \(\lambda^\top m_D\) whenever
\[
b_D=\lambda^\top A_D+\sum_{\omega\in Z_D(m_D)}\zeta_\omega e_\omega.
\]
If additionally \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, the membership is also necessary for constancy on \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\). On that focal-district-saturated active-slice-separated class, failure yields two compatible SCM families on the original alphabets \(\mathcal X\) that agree on every supplied law and disagree on the target cell, while every district \(D'\ne D\) retains its original graph-compatible restrictions. The structural predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) is sufficient for the active-slice hypothesis. For a problem outside this exact focal-projection scope, failure is only a local outer-relaxation witness.
statements.justification: Forced-zero coordinates define the active row space, which gives broad-fiber identification and an exact original-alphabet criterion once active-slice projection is available.
statements.gap: Raghavan and Bareinboim give graphical completeness for Layer-3 inputs, but not this boundary-face row-space characterization or its source-labelled active-slice realization theorem.
statements.consumer: A released menu that pins the focal response law to a simplex face can identify targets missed by ordinary row rank, including menus with cross-district cells whose focal slices are already controlled.
statements.proof_tex:
Write
\[
K=\mathcal K_D(m_D),\qquad A=A_D,\qquad m=m_D,
\qquad Z=Z_D(m_D),\qquad J=\Omega_D\setminus Z.
\]
For broad sufficiency, let \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).  By \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}district\text{-}fiber\text{-}projection}\), \(q_D^\star(\mathbf M)\in K\).  If
\[
b_D=\lambda^\top A+
\sum_{\omega\in Z}\zeta_\omega e_\omega,
\]
then
\[
\begin{aligned}
b_Dq_D^\star(\mathbf M)
&=\lambda^\top A q_D^\star(\mathbf M)
+\sum_{\omega\in Z}\zeta_\omega q_D^\star(\mathbf M)(\omega)\\
&=\lambda^\top m.
\end{aligned}
\]
The first term uses \(Aq_D^\star=m\); every term in the sum vanishes by the definition of \(Z\).  The coefficient matrix in the displayed decomposition has entries in \(\{0,1\}\), and \(b_D\) is also a zero--one row.  Rational Gaussian elimination therefore permits \(\lambda\) and the \(\zeta_\omega\) to be chosen rational whenever the decomposition is consistent.  By \(\mathrm{def:stacked\text{-}menu\text{-}system}\), the entries of \(m\) are supplied cells or certified extracted kernels; by \(\mathrm{def:typed\text{-}extraction\text{-}judgment}\), every division used by the latter has a certified nonzero denominator.  Hence \(\lambda^\top m\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\).  Thus the target equals an allowed rational functional of the supplied menu throughout the broad fiber.  This proves sufficiency without saturation or a separation hypothesis.

Now assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\).  The focal projection theorem gives
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=K,
\]
so \(K\ne\varnothing\).  Because \(A\) contains the normalization row, \(\mathbf 1^\top q=1\) for every \(q\in K\); hence \(J\ne\varnothing\).  For each \(\omega\in J\), the definition of \(Z\) supplies \(q^\omega\in K\) with \(q^\omega(\omega)>0\).  Therefore
\[
\bar q=\frac{1}{\lvert J\rvert}\sum_{\omega\in J}q^\omega
\]
belongs to \(K\), vanishes on \(Z\), and is strictly positive on every coordinate in \(J\).

Define
\[
L=\{v\in\mathbb R^{\Omega_D}:Av=0,
\ v(\omega)=0\text{ for every }\omega\in Z\}.
\]
If \(v\in L\), finiteness of \(J\) and strict positivity of \(\bar q\) on \(J\) permit \(\varepsilon>0\) such that
\[
\varepsilon\lvert v(\omega)\rvert
\leq\frac12\bar q(\omega)
\qquad(\omega\in J).
\]
Then \(\bar q\pm\varepsilon v\geq0\), both vectors vanish on \(Z\), and
\(A(\bar q\pm\varepsilon v)=m\); hence both belong to \(K\).  Conversely, the difference of any two points of \(K\) lies in \(L\).  It follows that \(L\) is exactly the direction space of the affine hull of \(K\).

Let \(\widetilde A\) append to \(A\) the coordinate rows \(e_\omega\) for \(\omega\in Z\).  Then \(L=\ker(\widetilde A)\).  Finite-dimensional row reduction gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
L^\perp
&=(\ker\widetilde A)^\perp
=\operatorname{row}(\widetilde A)\\
&=\operatorname{row}(A)+
\operatorname{span}\{e_\omega:\omega\in Z\}
=R_D(m_D).
\end{aligned}
\]
By the exact projection, the target is constant on the focal fiber if and only if the linear row \(b_D\) is constant on \(K\).  This holds if and only if \(b_Dv=0\) for every \(v\in L\), equivalently if and only if \(b_D\in L^\perp=R_D(m_D)\).  This proves necessity.

If membership fails, choose \(v\in L\) with \(b_Dv\ne0\) and then choose \(\varepsilon>0\) as above.  The two laws
\[
q_+=\bar q+\varepsilon v,
\qquad q_-=\bar q-\varepsilon v
\]
belong to \(K\) and satisfy
\[
b_Dq_+-b_Dq_-=2\varepsilon b_Dv\ne0.
\]
The focal projection theorem realizes them by \(\mathbf M_+,\mathbf M_-\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\) on the original alphabets.  Membership in the same compatibility fiber proves that these families agree on every supplied law, while the last display proves disagreement on the target cell.  The projection construction changes only the response law at \(D\), so all other districts retain their baseline graph-compatible restrictions.  By \(\mathrm{lem:structural\text{-}separation\text{-}implies\text{-}active\text{-}slice}\), the older \(\mathsf{Sep}_D\) condition remains a sufficient test for the exact clause.  Without the focal exact-projection hypotheses, the construction supplies only two points of the local row-face relaxation, not necessarily two compatible SCMs.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), each nonterminal \(\mathsf{NORM}\), \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\), \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\), \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\), \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\), \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\), or \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\) step preserves the ordered pair of root denotations pointwise. The preservation witnesses are respectively the checked normalization derivation, finite ancestor marginalization identity, checked district sum-product derivation, admissible extraction equations \(A_Dq_D^\star=m_D\), active-face calculation, finite additivity, and district factorization. The \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) rule labels its terminal with the same two root values and divides only under an independent strict-positivity certificate. In the rank \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}=(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi},r_C)\), the first seven rules respectively decrease \(r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi}\) while fixing every earlier coordinate, and \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) decreases \(r_C\) after the others vanish; no rule creates an earlier-phase node. The fixed priority and least-applicable-node convention give a unique successor. From a well-typed initial configuration, \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable because every declared partial-operation failure takes its specified \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) branch.
statements.justification: A typed operational semantics needs a local invariant for every transition before terminal soundness follows.
statements.gap: The prior transport recursions prove their own rule systems sound, but do not cover certified Layer-3 extraction from heterogeneous source-labelled laws.
statements.consumer: The local invariant supports independent checking of a returned derivation or failure trace.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). We verify the transition invariant in phase order.

For \(\mathsf{NORM}\), the attached derivation is a composition of consistency, unnesting, contradiction removal, Boolean disjoint-normal-form identities, and finite disjoint additivity. Each constructor preserves the event probability, so replacing the node preserves every root that reaches it. For \(\mathsf{ANCESTOR}\), the omitted variables range over their complete finite declared alphabets, and therefore
\[
P(e)=\sum_xP(e,x),
\]
which is the checked ancestor marginalization identity. For \(\mathsf{SPLIT}\), the compiler enumerates all assignments and the districts of \(G[H]\); \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\) identifies the ancestor-closed probability with the checked finite sum of products. Hence the first three transitions preserve both root denotations.

At \(\mathsf{EXTRACT}\), a retained raw row has a checked proof both of district locality and of \(s=\star\) or \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\). Typed-menu realizability and finite recursive evaluation give
\[
P_a^s(v)=r^{\mathrm{raw}}_{s,a,D,v}q_D^s.
\]
The admissibility proof and district-kernel invariance replace \(q_D^s\) by \(q_D^\star\). For every retained derived row, \(\mathrm{lem:district\text{-}cell\text{-}linearity}\) gives
\[
K_{s,a,D}(c\mid h)=r_{s,a,D,h,c}q_D^\star.
\]
Together with \(\mathbf 1^\top q_D^\star=1\), stacking all accepted equalities yields
\[
A_Dq_D^\star(\mathbf M)=m_D.
\]
Both the row-needed node and its face-needed successor denote \(bq_D^\star(\mathbf M)\), while rejected candidates create no asserted equality. Thus extraction preserves denotation.

At \(\mathsf{FACE\_ID}\), the exact certificate supplies
\[
b=\lambda^\top A+\sum_{\omega\in Z}\zeta_\omega e_\omega,
\qquad Aq_D^\star=m,
\qquad q_D^\star(\omega)=0\quad(\omega\in Z).
\]
Consequently
\[
bq_D^\star=\lambda^\top m,
\]
which is exactly the resolved-node denotation. This calculation uses only inclusion of the global projection in the row face, not surjectivity onto that face. The \(\mathsf{MARGINALIZE}\) transition preserves denotation by finite additivity, and \(\mathsf{PRODUCT}\) preserves it by district factorization. This proves pointwise preservation for all seven nonterminal transformation rules.

The \(\mathsf{CONDITION}\) transition records the same resolved numerator and denominator. It constructs a quotient only when the independent certificate \(\pi\) proves strict positivity throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\); the zero and failure branches perform no division.

For the operational assertions, the first seven rules respectively decrease
\[
r_N,r_A,r_S,r_X,r_F,r_{\Sigma},r_{\Pi}
\]
while fixing all earlier coordinates of \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}\), and no rule creates an earlier-phase node. Condition decreases \(r_C\) after the other coordinates vanish. Fixed priority, canonical finite orders, and the least-applicable-node convention therefore select at most one successor. Conversely, a well-typed nonterminal configuration has a least unresolved phase; its rule either applies or invokes the specified typed failure constructor for the failed partial operation. Hence \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable.

statements.statement: For every realizable typed menu with \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), the priority transition system \(\mathsf{DCTFTR}\) has a unique finite run because \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}\in\mathbb N^8\) decreases lexicographically. Every reached configuration has root denotation \((P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\wedge E),P_{M^\star}(E))\) for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). If the result is \(\operatorname{ID}(\operatorname{Quot}(F_B,F_E,\pi),\delta_B,\delta_E,\pi)\), then \(F_B,F_E\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P)\), \(\pi\) proves \(F_E>0\) throughout \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), and \(F_B(\mathcal P)/F_E(\mathcal P)=Q_\rho^\star(\mathbf M)\) for every compatible model. If \(z\) proves \(F_E=0\) throughout the fiber, the result is \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\) and the conditional is undefined. A split failure, failed extraction, normalization-only face failure, denominator witness at zero, or uncertified denominator positivity returns its typed \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) trace and performs no division. A \(\operatorname{FACE\_NOT\_IDENTIFIED}\) witness certifies only local district-face variation and implies global nonidentification only when the hypotheses of the one-district fiber-projection theorem are separately verified. The observed numerical sign of \(F_E\) is never itself a positivity certificate, and \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable from a well-typed initial configuration.
statements.justification: The source-labelled Layer-3 recursion must be valid before its output can enter the sharper arm-ordering analysis.
statements.gap: CTFTR handles heterogeneous Layer-1/2 inputs and CTFIDU+ handles one-specification Layer-3 inputs; neither soundness argument covers both features simultaneously.
statements.consumer: A successful output can be evaluated directly from released source tables, while impossible conditioning events are rejected before division.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{def:dctftr\text{-}recursion}\), for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) the initial roots denote
\[
\bigl(P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\cap E),P_{M^\star}(E)\bigr).
\]
Induction over the checked trace, applying \(\mathrm{lem:dctftr\text{-}transition\text{-}preservation}\) at every nonterminal step, proves that every reached configuration has this same ordered pair of root denotations.

The lexicographic order on \(\mathbb N^8\) is well founded: nested induction on the first coordinate, then the second, and so on excludes an infinite sequence that fixes all earlier coordinates and strictly decreases the first coordinate at which it changes. Every nonterminal transition has this property by the transition-preservation lemma. Hence the run is finite. Fixed priority and the least-node convention give at most one successor; the phase analysis in that lemma gives either that successor or a typed terminal. The run is unique, and \(\operatorname{STUCK}\) is unreachable from a well-typed initial configuration.

Suppose the terminal is
\[
\operatorname{ID}(\operatorname{Quot}(F_B,F_E,\pi),\delta_B,\delta_E,\pi).
\]
The expression grammar starts from typed-menu cells and rational constants and is closed under precisely the finite sums, products, and certified quotients used by the transitions. Induction over \(\delta_B\) and \(\delta_E\) therefore gives
\[
F_B,F_E\in\mathscr R(\mathcal P).
\]
Root preservation gives, for every compatible \(\mathbf M\),
\[
F_B(\mathcal P)=P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\cap E),
\qquad
F_E(\mathcal P)=P_{M^\star}(E).
\]
The independent certificate \(\pi\) proves \(F_E>0\) throughout the compatibility fiber. Division is thus well typed, and
\[
\frac{F_B(\mathcal P)}{F_E(\mathcal P)}
=\frac{P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\cap E)}{P_{M^\star}(E)}
=P_{M^\star}(B_\rho\mid E)
=Q_\rho^\star(\mathbf M).
\]

If the independent zero calculus proves \(z:F_E=0\) throughout the fiber, evidence has probability zero in every compatible model, so the conditional is undefined and the terminal is \(\operatorname{ZERO\_EVIDENCE}(F_E,z)\). Every other listed failure is returned exactly where a required typed judgment or certificate is absent and performs no division. In particular, the numerical sign of one evaluated denominator is not used as a uniform positivity certificate. A face-failure vector varies only the relaxation \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\); it is a global paired-model certificate only when the nonempty district-saturated compatibility fiber and separation hypotheses independently establish exact projection onto that face.

statements.statement: Under the finite semi-Markovian convention, the observational and atomic hard-interventional restriction \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFTR}}\) has a proper typed embedding into \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{DCTFTR}}\). The DCTFTR-expressible intersection \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFIDU+}}\) of the published one-SCM Layer-3 grammar has a proper typed embedding obtained by setting \(\mathcal S=\{\star\}\) and applying its declared constructor map. No embedding of the full CTFTR conditional or stochastic-policy grammar, and no embedding of an undeclared CTFIDU+ Layer-2.5 action, is asserted. On either embedded restriction, every successful DCTFTR functional and every successful functional returned by the corresponding published calculus equals the same causal query in every compatible model; syntactic or transition-by-transition equivalence is not asserted. In \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\), the first restriction cannot accept the genuine cross-world cell \(p\), while the complete source-labelled family with \(P^\star(Z=1)=0\) and \(P^s(Z=1)=1\) is not realizable by one SCM and hence is outside the second restriction.
statements.justification: Typed proper embeddings state exactly which published input classes are recovered and where the multi-domain Layer-3 language is strictly larger.
statements.gap: CTFTR and CTFIDU+ occupy different proper subgrammars; neither accepts the complete binary multi-domain instance.
statements.consumer: Users can recognize settled CTFTR and CTFIDU+ cases while reserving DCTFTR for genuinely heterogeneous Layer-3 inputs.
statements.proof_tex:
By definition, \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFTR}}\) retains only observational and atomic hard-interventional constructors that are also constructors of the DCTFTR typed-menu grammar. Sending the graph, each domain label, descriptor, supplied law, and query to the identically labelled DCTFTR object is therefore injective and type preserving. The conditional and stochastic-policy constructors excluded from this restricted carrier are not mapped.

Likewise, \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{CTFIDU+}}\) is the one-domain intersection for which a constructor map into the DCTFTR partial-copy syntax is explicitly declared. Set \(\mathcal S=\{\star\}\), send each action through that declared map, and retain the graph, supplied cells, and target. This is injective and type preserving. No action lacking the constructor map is used.

On either image, \(\mathrm{thm:recursion\text{-}soundness}\) proves that every successful DCTFTR expression equals the causal query in every compatible model. The already established nodes \(\mathrm{lem:ctftr\text{-}published\text{-}soundness}\) and \(\mathrm{lem:ctfiduplus\text{-}published\text{-}soundness}\) give the same semantic equality for a successful published expression on the corresponding input restriction. Thus successful expressions agree with the same query; no equality of syntax or traces is needed.

Both embeddings are proper. In \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\),
\[
p=P^s(Y_0=1,Y_1=1)=\frac38
\]
is a joint cross-world cell, not an observational or atomic hard-interventional descriptor, so the first restricted carrier does not contain the instance. For the second carrier, a one-SCM instance has one factual law for \(Z\), whereas the binary family requires simultaneously
\[
P^\star(Z=1)=0,
\qquad
P^s(Z=1)=1.
\]
No single probability law satisfies both equations. The two-domain DCTFTR family permits the difference because \(Z\in\Delta_s\). Hence the binary instance lies in \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{DCTFTR}}\) but outside each embedded restriction.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\) and \(d_Dq>0\) for every \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). Then
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)=
\max_{\eta\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(A_D)}}
\{m_D^\top\eta:A_D^\top\eta\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\}.
\]
Every feasible dual vector with \(m_D^\top\eta>0\) certifies \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) in every model in the broad fiber \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\). If additionally \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, this certificate condition is also necessary for uniform strict dominance on the focal-district-saturated fiber. Under these additional hypotheses, \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0\) is attained by an original-alphabet compatible focal-district-saturated SCM with \(Q_\sigma^\star<Q_\rho^\star\), and \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0<\overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)\) yields two such SCM families with opposite strict rankings while preserving every other district's graph-compatible restrictions. The structural predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) remains sufficient for the active-slice hypothesis. Without the additional hypotheses, the primal optimizers need not lift from the row face.
statements.justification: The theorem gives an auditable broad-fiber certificate and exact opposing focal-district SCMs whenever the row-face optimum reverses sign and active-slice projection applies.
statements.gap: Park and Lee's CTF-POMIS is graph based and PATR supplies valid Layer-1/2 transported bounds; neither derives this heterogeneous Layer-3 dual certificate with active-slice fixed-alphabet lifting.
statements.consumer: A bandit analyst can audit strict removal by source-table weights and recover a countermodel without altering any nonfocal district.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(K=\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) and \(g=g_{\rho,\sigma,D}\).  The normalization row of \(A_D\) gives \(\mathbf 1^\top q=1\) for every \(q\in K\).  Thus the assumed nonempty set \(K\) is a closed subset of the finite probability simplex, hence compact, and its linear minimum and maximum are attained.

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}linear\text{-}programming\text{-}strong\text{-}duality}\) with primal variable \(q\), equality constraint \(A_Dq=m_D\), nonnegativity constraint \(q\geq0\), and cost row \(g\).  The equality multiplier \(\eta\) is unrestricted, while the nonnegative primal coordinates give the dual constraint \(A_D^\top\eta\leq g^\top\).  Therefore
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)
=\min_{q\in K}gq
=\max_{\eta:A_D^\top\eta\leq g^\top}m_D^\top\eta.
\]
For every primal-feasible \(q\) and dual-feasible \(\eta\), weak duality is also the direct calculation
\[
m_D^\top\eta
=q^\top A_D^\top\eta
\leq gq.
\tag{2}
\]

Let \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).  The broad projection theorem gives \(q=q_D^\star(\mathbf M)\in K\).  If a feasible \(\eta\) has \(m_D^\top\eta>0\), (2) gives \(gq>0\).  The stated denominator condition gives \(d_Dq>0\), so \(\mathrm{lem:district\text{-}cell\text{-}linearity}\) and the definition \(g=n_{\sigma,D}-n_{\rho,D}\) give
\[
Q_\sigma^\star(\mathbf M)-Q_\rho^\star(\mathbf M)
=\frac{n_{\sigma,D}q-n_{\rho,D}q}{d_Dq}
=\frac{gq}{d_Dq}>0.
\]
Thus every positive dual certificate is sound on the broad fiber.  Division occurs only after the assumed strict positivity has been invoked.

Now also assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\).  The focal projection theorem gives \(\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=K\).  Since the denominator is positive throughout \(K\), uniform strict dominance on the focal fiber is equivalent to \(gq>0\) for every \(q\in K\).  Compactness of \(K\) and continuity of \(q\mapsto gq\) make this equivalent to
\[
\min_{q\in K}gq>0.
\]
Dual attainment makes the last inequality equivalent to existence of a feasible \(\eta\) with \(m_D^\top\eta>0\), proving necessity.

If \(\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)<0\), an attained minimizer \(q_-\in K\) has \(gq_-<0\).  Focal projection realizes \(q_-\) by an original-alphabet family in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\), and positivity of \(d_Dq_-\) gives \(Q_\sigma^\star<Q_\rho^\star\).  If also \(\overline\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(m_D)>0\), an attained maximizer \(q_+\in K\) is realized in the same way and satisfies \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\).  Both families induce \(\mathcal P\); the focal realization changes only district \(D\), so their other districts retain the baseline graph-compatible restrictions.  Structural separation is sufficient here by \(\mathrm{lem:structural\text{-}separation\text{-}implies\text{-}active\text{-}slice}\).  Without focal saturation and active-slice separation, an optimizer of the outer row face need not be induced by a graph-compatible SCM, so no converse lifting is asserted.

statements.statement: Suppose \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\ne\varnothing\) and \(d_Dq>0\) throughout \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). For every realizable additional row \(r_D^\dagger\), the feasible set \(I_D\) is a closed interval and \(p\mapsto\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)\) is a finite convex piecewise-affine function. Its pieces may be obtained from feasible bases of the row-augmented dual program and have coefficients that are rational affine functions of \(m_D\). Hence \(\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+\) is the complement in \(I_D\) of a closed convex subset, which is empty, a point, or a closed interval, and has zero, one, or two relative sign boundaries. Each boundary has a dual menu-weight certificate of value zero and a primal row-face law attaining equality; the adjacent strict-pruning side has a positive dual piece. If the supplied menu augmented by the boundary equality \(r_D^\dagger q=p\) has a nonempty focal-district-saturated compatibility fiber and satisfies its \(\mathsf{ASep}_D\) predicate, the equality law is realized by an SCM saturated only at \(D\) on the original alphabets \(\mathcal X\), with every district \(D'\ne D\) retaining its original graph-compatible restrictions. The structural predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D\) is a sufficient check for this active-slice condition. Without those hypotheses, no SCM lifting of the row-face boundary is asserted.
statements.justification: This gives the exact parametric Layer-3 sign boundary and realizes boundary laws whenever the augmented menu satisfies active-slice separation.
statements.gap: The located identification papers treat a fixed menu, and the Park--Lee bandit papers do not give a parametric Layer-3 cell diagram with active-slice focal-district boundary SCMs.
statements.consumer: A study designer can identify realized partial-copy cell values that justify pruning and obtain a boundary SCM without relaxing irrelevant districts.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(K=\mathcal K_D(m_D)\), \(r=r_D^\dagger\), and \(g=g_{\rho,\sigma,D}\).  The normalization row makes \(K\) a nonempty compact convex polytope in the finite probability simplex.  Its image under the linear map \(q\mapsto rq\) is therefore a nonempty compact convex subset of \(\mathbb R\), hence a closed interval \(I_D\).  For every \(p\in I_D\),
\[
K(p)=\{q\in K:rq=p\}
\]
is nonempty and compact, so the defining minimum of \(gq\) is attained.

Let \(p_0,p_1\in I_D\), choose minimizers \(q_i\in K(p_i)\), and let \(0\leq t\leq1\).  Then \(tq_0+(1-t)q_1\in K(tp_0+(1-t)p_1)\), whence
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(tp_0+(1-t)p_1;m_D)
\leq t\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p_0;m_D)
+(1-t)\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p_1;m_D).
\]
Thus the value function is convex.

Append \(r\) to \(A_D\) and apply \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}linear\text{-}programming\text{-}strong\text{-}duality}\) to the nonempty bounded fiber \(K(p)\).  It gives
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)
=\max_{(\eta,\beta):A_D^\top\eta+\beta r^\top\leq g^\top}
\{m_D^\top\eta+\beta p\}.
\tag{3}
\]
The dual feasible polyhedron is independent of \((m_D,p)\) and is cut out by finitely many rational inequalities, because \(A_D\), \(r\), and \(g\) have integer entries.  Let
\[
L_0=\{(u,t):A_D^\top u+t r^\top=0\}
\]
be its lineality space.  If \(p\in I_D\) and \(q\in K(p)\), then for \((u,t)\in L_0\),
\[
m_D^\top u+tp
=q^\top(A_D^\top u+t r^\top)=0.
\]
Hence the objective in (3) is constant on cosets of \(L_0\) and descends to the quotient polyhedron.  Choose a rational linear complement to the rational space \(L_0\).  In that complement the quotient is a pointed rational polyhedron with finitely many vertices.  Strong duality says its linear objective has a finite attained maximum for every \(p\in I_D\).  An attained maximum of a linear functional on a pointed polyhedron is attained at a vertex: if an optimal face contained no vertex, it would contain a line, contradicting pointedness.  Enumerating its finitely many vertices gives rational pairs \((\eta_B,\beta_B)\), indexed by feasible bases \(B\), such that
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)
=\max_B\{m_D^\top\eta_B+\beta_Bp\}
\qquad(p\in I_D).
\tag{4}
\]
Thus the value is finite, continuous, convex, and piecewise affine.  Each slope \(\beta_B\) is rational, and each intercept \(m_D^\top\eta_B\) is rational linear, hence rational affine, in \(m_D\).

The sublevel set
\[
N=\{p\in I_D:\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)\leq0\}
\]
is closed by continuity and convex by convexity.  A closed convex subset of a real interval is empty, a point, or a closed interval, with the whole interval allowed in the last case.  Its relative complement is \(\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+\), so there are zero, one, or two relative sign boundaries.  At any such boundary \(p_\partial\), continuity gives
\[
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p_\partial;m_D)=0.
\]
Primal attainment supplies \(q_\partial\in K(p_\partial)\) with \(gq_\partial=0\).  By (4), only finitely many dual pieces occur.  Along a sequence in an adjacent positive component converging to \(p_\partial\), some active piece recurs on a subsequence.  Its affine value is positive on that subsequence and converges to zero at the boundary.  Its feasibility is independent of \(p\), so the same pair \((\eta_B,\beta_B)\) is a zero-valued dual menu certificate at \(p_\partial\) and a positive certificate on the adjacent piece.

Finally augment the supplied menu by the equality \(rq=p_\partial\).  If the augmented menu has nonempty focal-district-saturated compatibility fiber and satisfies \(\mathsf{ASep}_D\), the focal projection theorem for its augmented row system realizes \(q_\partial\) by an original-alphabet compatible SCM saturated only at \(D\).  The stated condition \(d_Dq_\partial>0\) permits division and gives
\[
Q_\sigma^\star-Q_\rho^\star
=\frac{gq_\partial}{d_Dq_\partial}=0.
\]
The realization changes no other district's graph-compatible structure.  The implication \(\mathsf{Sep}_D\Rightarrow\mathsf{ASep}_D\) makes structural separation a sufficient check.  Without the focal saturation and active-slice hypotheses, primal attainment supplies only a boundary point of the row-face relaxation, not an SCM lifting.

statements.statement: For \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{bin}}\), the base face has the unique parameterization \(q(p)=(p,1/2-p,1/2-p,p)\), \(0\le p\le1/2\), and \[Q_\rho(q(p))=1-2p,\qquad Q_\sigma(q(p))=1/2,\qquad I_D=[0,1/2],\qquad \Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)=2p-1/2,\qquad \mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+=(1/4,1/2].\] With the augmented row order consisting of the three rows of \(A_D\) followed by \(r_D^\dagger\), the dual vector \((0,-1,0,2)^\top\) represents \(g_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) exactly and has value \(2p-1/2\); at the realized value \(p=3/8\) it certifies margin \(1/4\). The boundary SCM is \(q(1/4)=(1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4)\), while \(q(0)\) makes \(\rho\) strictly optimal and \(q(1/2)\) makes \(\sigma\) strictly optimal on the original binary alphabets. For the sole unit-cost block, \[\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\{\rho,\sigma\},\qquad \mathcal K_{\{e^\dagger\}}=\{q(3/8)\},\qquad \operatorname{PO}(\{e^\dagger\})=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.\] The first equality is witnessed by \(p=0\) for \(\rho\) and \(p=1/2\) for \(\sigma\); at \(p=3/8\), \(Q_\sigma=1/2>1/4=Q_\rho\), and no other arm exists because \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\).
statements.justification: This exhaustive binary calculation verifies the sign frontier, the dual certificate, the boundary law, and the decision consequence in one complete instance.
statements.gap: The published identification and bandit papers do not exhibit a heterogeneous genuine Layer-3 cell whose observed value crosses an exact transported pruning boundary.
statements.consumer: The instance is a regression test for extraction, face identification, experiment blocking, and undefined-arm-safe pruning.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(q=(q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4)^\top\) in the response-profile order of \(\mathrm{def:binary\text{-}check}\). The equations \(A_Dq=m_D\) are
\[
q_1+q_2+q_3+q_4=1,
\qquad q_3+q_4=\frac12,
\qquad q_2+q_4=\frac12,
\qquad q_j\geq0.
\]
Setting \(p=q_4\) gives
\[
q_1=p,
\qquad q_2=q_3=\frac12-p,
\qquad 0\leq p\leq\frac12,
\]
which proves the unique parameterization \(q(p)\). Since \(d_Dq(p)=1\), direct row multiplication gives
\[
Q_\rho(q(p))=q_2+q_3=1-2p,
\qquad
Q_\sigma(q(p))=q_2+q_4=\frac12.
\]
The candidate row gives \(r_D^\dagger q(p)=q_4=p\), so
\[
I_D=[0,1/2],
\qquad
\Gamma_{\rho\prec\sigma}(p;m_D)
=g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q(p)=-q_3+q_4=2p-\frac12,
\]
and therefore \(\mathcal J_{\rho\prec\sigma}^+=(1/4,1/2]\).

In the augmented row order,
\[
(0,-1,0,2)
\begin{bmatrix}A_D\\ r_D^\dagger\end{bmatrix}
=(0,0,-1,1)=g_{\rho,\sigma,D}.
\]
The vector is dual feasible with equality, and its objective is
\[
(0,-1,0,2)(1,1/2,1/2,p)^\top=2p-\frac12.
\]
At \(p=3/8\) this value is \(1/4\).

For every \(p\in[0,1/2]\), let a binary response-block variable \(U_Y\) have profile law \(q(p)\), and set \(Y_t=f_t(U_Y)\) for \(t\in\{0,1\}\). Use the same \(U_Y\) law in target and source because \(D=\{Y\}\) is unchanged. Let \(Z=0\) deterministically in the target and \(Z=1\) deterministically in the source, and choose an independent treatment mechanism. The system is recursive, all observed outputs remain binary, exogenous blocks of distinct singleton districts are independent, \(\Delta_s=\{Z\}\) is district closed, and the response law of \(Y\) is invariant. Thus
\[
q(1/4)=(1/4,1/4,1/4,1/4),
\quad q(0)=(0,1/2,1/2,0),
\quad q(1/2)=(1/2,0,0,1/2)
\]
are realized on the original binary alphabets and have gaps \(0,-1/2,1/2\), respectively.

With no experiment, \(p=0\) makes \(\rho\) strictly optimal and \(p=1/2\) makes \(\sigma\) strictly optimal, so
\[
\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\{\rho,\sigma\}.
\]
Acquiring the sole block imposes \(q_4=3/8\), and the unique parameterization gives
\[
\mathcal K_{\{e^\dagger\}}=\{q(3/8)\}.
\]
At this law \(Q_\rho=1/4<1/2=Q_\sigma\). Since \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}=\{\rho,\sigma\}\),
\[
\operatorname{PO}(\{e^\dagger\})=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.
\]

statements.statement: Suppose the reduced arm comparison has one district \(D\). If there exists \(\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\) with \(A_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}\le g_{\rho,\sigma,D}^\top\) and \(m_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}>0\), removing \(\rho\) cannot remove a maximizing arm from \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{arm}}\); an arm whose common evidence is certified zero is excluded as undefined rather than ranked.
statements.justification: This records the elementary decision consequence while keeping it out of the research kernel.
statements.gap: The exclusion rule itself is elementary and is not positioned as a strengthening of Park and Lee; the new content is the derived sharp certificate in Theorems 5 and 6.
statements.consumer: A counterfactual bandit can initialize exploration on the certificate-retained action set without treating undefined conditionals as low rewards.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\) and set \(q=q_D^\star(\mathbf M)\). District-cell linearity and the stacking construction give \(q\in\mathcal K_D(m_D)\). Feasibility of the stated dual vector gives
\[
g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q
\geq q^\top A_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}
=m_D^\top\eta_{\rho,\sigma,D}>0.
\]
Because \(n_{\rho,D}\) and \(n_{\sigma,D}\) are incidence rows of subevents of the common evidence event,
\[
0\leq n_{\rho,D}\leq d_D,
\qquad 0\leq n_{\sigma,D}\leq d_D
\]
coordinatewise. Hence
\[
d_Dq\geq n_{\sigma,D}q
=g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q+n_{\rho,D}q>0.
\]
Both conditional values are defined, and
\[
Q_\sigma(q)-Q_\rho(q)
=\frac{g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q}{d_Dq}>0.
\]
Thus \(\rho\) is strictly dominated by the available arm \(\sigma\) in every compatible model and cannot maximize the arm value; removing it cannot remove a maximizing arm. If an independent certificate instead proves that the common evidence has probability zero, recursion soundness declares the conditional undefined. Exclusion in that case is a domain-of-definition decision, not a ranking of an undefined reward.

statements.statement:
For every finite instance, all minimum-cost Layer-3 regime-block solutions are characterized by enumerating \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\) and, for each arm, solving the finite linear program consisting of the equations defining \(\mathcal K_S\), the common-denominator positivity test, and the pairwise numerator-gap inequalities. This is an algorithmic computation whenever all matrix entries, menu values, and costs are effectively presented rational or real algebraic numbers. In general the elimination function \(f\) is not submodular. In particular, there is a realizable one-domain binary one-district instance with two unit-cost Layer-3 cell experiments for which
\[
\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1\})
=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_2\})=\{\rho,\sigma\},
\qquad
\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1,e_2\})=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}.
\]
Consequently the marginal gain of \(e_2\) is zero at \(S=\varnothing\) and one at \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}=\{e_1\}\), violating diminishing returns. For this instance the exact acquisition problem is
\[
\min_{x_1,x_2\in\{0,1\}}x_1+x_2
\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1+x_2\geq2,
\]
whose unique solution is \((x_1,x_2)=(1,1)\) with cost two. The multiplier \(y=1\) for the covering inequality is a matching dual lower-bound certificate for the continuous relaxation.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(S\subseteq\mathcal U\). The set \(\mathcal K_S\) is described by the finitely many equations
\[
A_Dq=m_D,
\qquad R_eq=p_e\quad(e\in S),
\]
and the inequalities \(q\geq0\). For a candidate arm \(\rho\), whenever the common denominator is positive,
\[
Q_\rho(q)\geq Q_\sigma(q)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(n_{\rho,D}-n_{\sigma,D})q\geq0.
\]
Therefore \(\rho\in\operatorname{PO}(S)\) exactly when the linear program that maximizes \(d_Dq\) over \(q\in\mathcal K_S\) subject to all pairwise numerator-gap inequalities has a strictly positive optimum. This gives a finite LP characterization for every arm and every \(S\). Enumerating the finite set of \(2^{|\mathcal U|}\) subsets, comparing each \(\operatorname{PO}(S)\) with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), and minimizing \(\sum_{e\in S}c_e\) characterizes every minimum-cost solution. If the coefficients are effectively rational or real algebraic, exact ordered-field arithmetic and finite LP pivoting decide each equality, inequality, and strict positivity test, so the characterization is algorithmic. No such effective assertion is made for an uneffectively specified real coefficient.

For the non-submodularity witness, take the binary graph \(T_{\mathrm{tr}}\to Y\), the singleton district \(D=\{Y\}\), sure evidence, and response-profile order
\[
\Omega_D=((0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)).
\]
Let the base face be the whole simplex. Let \(\rho\) be treatment zero and \(\sigma\) treatment one, with reward \(Y=1\). Then
\[
n_{\rho,D}=(0,0,1,1),
\qquad n_{\sigma,D}=(0,1,0,1),
\qquad g_{\rho,\sigma,D}=(0,1,-1,0).
\]
Choose the realizable response law
\[
q^\star=(1/4,3/8,1/8,1/4).
\]
Experiment \(e_1\) reveals the Layer-3 cell \(q_2=P(Y_0=0,Y_1=1)=3/8\), and \(e_2\) reveals \(q_3=P(Y_0=1,Y_1=0)=1/8\); each has unit cost. A one-district response-block SCM with law \(q^\star\) realizes both cells on the original binary alphabets.

With no experiment, simplex laws with \(q_2-q_3<0\) and with \(q_2-q_3>0\) exist. Under \(e_1\) alone, the feasible pairs
\[
(q_2,q_3)=(3/8,5/8),
\qquad (q_2,q_3)=(3/8,0)
\]
have opposite gap signs. Under \(e_2\) alone, the feasible pairs
\[
(q_2,q_3)=(0,1/8),
\qquad (q_2,q_3)=(7/8,1/8)
\]
also have opposite signs. In each display the remaining nonnegative mass is assigned to coordinate one or four, whose gap coefficient is zero. The one-district response-block construction realizes every displayed law. Consequently
\[
\operatorname{PO}(\varnothing)=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1\})
=\operatorname{PO}(\{e_2\})=\{\rho,\sigma\}.
\]
With both blocks, every feasible law satisfies
\[
g_{\rho,\sigma,D}q=q_2-q_3=\frac38-\frac18=\frac14>0,
\]
so \(\operatorname{PO}(\{e_1,e_2\})=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}=\{\sigma\}\). Hence
\[
f(\{e_2\})-f(\varnothing)=0
<1=f(\{e_1,e_2\})-f(\{e_1\}),
\]
which violates diminishing returns for \(S=\varnothing\), \(T_{\mathrm{exp}}=\{e_1\}\), and \(e=e_2\).

Omitting either experiment leaves both arms possibly optimal by the displayed witnesses. Full-information pruning therefore requires both acquisition variables, and the exact integer program is
\[
\min_{x_1,x_2\in\{0,1\}}x_1+x_2
\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1+x_2\geq2.
\]
Its unique feasible optimum is \((1,1)\) with value two. For every point of the continuous relaxation, the covering constraint itself gives \(x_1+x_2\geq2\); multiplying it by \(y=1\) is a valid dual lower bound of two, matching the feasible point \((1,1)\).

statements.statement: Under the frozen transport assumptions, district closure has no nontrivial strictly weaker graph-only replacement for a partially selected district.  More precisely, omit district closure while retaining district-kernel invariance exactly as stated, and let \(0<|D\cap\Delta_s|<|D|\).  Then every nonconstant binary incidence row on \(\Omega_D\) admits two finite original-alphabet SCM families having identical supplied source laws but different target values of that row.  Hence, based on a source row alone, the universally transportable rows are exactly the constant rows.  If one additionally assumes invariance of the marginal response law on \(I=D\setminus\Delta_s\), then a row transports for every compatible pair if and only if it is constant on every fiber of the coordinate projection \(\Omega_D\to\Omega_I\); this condition is decidable by finite enumeration, and failure gives a two-point leakage certificate.
statements.proof_tex:
Retain district-kernel invariance with its frozen antecedent.  When
\(
 0<|D\cap\Delta_s|<|D|
\), that antecedent \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\) is false, so the assumption imposes no equality at all between \(q_D^s\) and \(q_D^\star\).  This is the obstruction: the graph and the partial selection set alone do not specify any invariant within-district response marginal.

Let \(r\in\{0,1\}^{\Omega_D}\) be nonconstant.  Choose \(\omega_0,\omega_1\in\Omega_D\) with \(r(\omega_0)=0\) and \(r(\omega_1)=1\).  Construct two source-labelled families as follows.  In both families use the same source response law \(q_D^s=\delta_{\omega_0}\), so every supplied source law, including the cell \(rq_D^s=0\), is identical.  Use no informative target menu row beyond normalization.  In the first family take \(q_D^\star=\delta_{\omega_0}\); in the second take \(q_D^\star=\delta_{\omega_1}\).  Extend each deterministic profile at unvisited parent configurations by any fixed value in the declared nonempty alphabet, and retain identical deterministic response blocks in every other district and domain.
