These are finite recursive SCMs on \(\mathcal X\), district factorization holds because the other district blocks are fixed independently, and the unchanged frozen kernel-invariance conditions hold in every wholly unselected district.  On the partially selected district they impose no restriction.  The two target values are
\[
 r\delta_{\omega_0}=0,
 \qquad r\delta_{\omega_1}=1.
\]
Thus every nonconstant source row has an original-alphabet paired-SCM leakage witness.  A constant row plainly has the same expectation under all probability laws, proving the asserted exact characterization under the frozen assumptions with closure removed.

For completeness, suppose a genuinely new marginal-kernel premise is stated explicitly:
\[
 (\mathrm{KMI})\qquad (\pi_I)_\#q_D^s=(\pi_I)_\#q_D^\star,
 \qquad I=D\setminus\Delta_s,
\]
where \(\pi_I\) restricts a district response profile to the response maps on \(I\).  If \(r=\widetilde r\circ\pi_I\), then
\[
 rq_D^s
 =\sum_{u\in\Omega_I}\widetilde r(u)(\pi_I)_\#q_D^s(u)
 =\sum_{u\in\Omega_I}\widetilde r(u)(\pi_I)_\#q_D^\star(u)
 =rq_D^\star,
\]
so the row transports.  Conversely, if \(r\) is not constant on a fiber, choose \(\omega_0,\omega_1\) in that fiber with different row values.  The laws \(\delta_{\omega_0}\) and \(\delta_{\omega_1}\) have the same \(\pi_I\)-marginal but different \(r\)-expectations, giving a two-point leakage certificate.  Testing all pairs of profiles with equal \(\pi_I\) is finite.  This proves both necessity and sufficiency under \((\mathrm{KMI})\), while also showing why \((\mathrm{KMI})\), which is absent from the frozen core, cannot be inferred from the graph alone.

statements.statement:
There are two exact finite frontiers with different scopes.

First, assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\). Then \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and, for every finite collection \(\mathcal F\) of declared target-domain counterfactual cells,
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Psi_C^\star(\theta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
Every \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine in the district response-law blocks and has total degree at most the number of districts visited by \(C\). Every point of the right-hand range is realized by a district-saturated SCM family on the original observed alphabets \(\mathcal X\).

Second, for an arbitrary acyclic directed mixed graph, if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) is a nonempty compact semialgebraic set and
\[
\{(P_{M^\star}(C):C\in\mathcal F):\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\}
=
\{(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star):C\in\mathcal F):
\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\}.
\]
The canonical realization also uses the original observed alphabets and retains the internal latent-factor restrictions of \(G\).

For either exact row
\[
(\mathfrak C,\Lambda,\Xi)
\in
\{(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P),\Theta(\mathcal P),\Psi),
(\mathcal C(\mathcal P),\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P),\Phi_{\mathrm{can}})\},
\]
provided \(\mathfrak C\ne\varnothing\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_T^\star(x^\star)
\]
are respectively the attained sharp lower and upper bounds for the target cell. At least one bound is strictly inside the logical interval \([0,1]\) exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one, and the cell is identified exactly when the two extrema agree. If the extrema differ, minimizing and maximizing realizations give two original-alphabet same-menu SCM families attaining different endpoint values. No assertion is made that every scalar value between the two extrema is attained. These are finite semialgebraic characterizations.

For the same row let
\[
e_-(\Lambda)=\min_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star),
\qquad
e_+(\Lambda)=\max_{x\in\Lambda}\Xi_E^\star(x^\star).
\]
If \(e_+(\Lambda)=0\), evidence is zero throughout \(\mathfrak C\); if \(e_-(\Lambda)=0<e_+(\Lambda)\), positivity is not uniform. In either case a conditional functional on all of \(\mathfrak C\) is rejected before division. If \(e_-(\Lambda)>0\), the quantities
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{x\in\Lambda}
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
are the attained sharp lower and upper conditional bounds. If they differ, their endpoint models are distinct; no interval-filling property of the conditional image is asserted. Under this positivity condition, \(Q_\sigma^\star>Q_\rho^\star\) throughout \(\mathfrak C\) if and only if
\[
\min_{x\in\Lambda}
\{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)\}>0,
\]
and opposite strict rankings occur in two same-menu original-alphabet models if and only if the minimum of the displayed gap is negative and its maximum is positive. Thus this strict minimum is the exact safe-pruning certificate for the chosen fiber.

Finally, for every district \(D\),
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
If \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds, the one-district fiber-projection theorem gives the exact local equality
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D),
\]
which requires saturation only of the focal district and preserves the graph-compatible restrictions of all \(D'\ne D\). Cross-district coupling of a complete supplied cell does not by itself defeat this equality: it is harmless whenever each fixed-nonfocal focal slice lies in \(R_D(m_D)\). The older structural predicate \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) is sufficient but not necessary for this active-slice condition. Outside focal-district saturation and active-slice separation, \(\mathcal K_D(m_D)\) is certified only as an outer relaxation. This local equality is distinct from the first, all-district-saturated global row, whose Cartesian district variation is what makes the displayed multi-affine program exact. Consequently a failed local face test is not a global nonidentification certificate outside the focal projection theorem's scope; distinct endpoint optimizers of the appropriate exact global program are the paired-model certificate whenever their objective values differ.
statements.justification: The theorem separates exact all-district multi-affine variation, exact sparse canonical optimization, and exact active-slice focal-district geometry.
statements.gap: Global programs retain every cross-district polynomial equality; locally, such coupling is also preserved when every fixed-nonfocal focal indicator slice belongs to the active row space.
statements.consumer: Global target bounds and arm pruning use attained exact-program optimizers, while local LP certificates use focal saturation plus the weaker active-slice condition.
statements.proof_tex:
We prove the two exact finite range equalities separately and then derive their optimization consequences.

First assume \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and take \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\).  For every domain \(s\) and district \(D\), push the law of the full response block \(U_D^s\in\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\) forward to the profile coordinates \(\Omega_D\) visited by the declared menus and target cells; call the resulting law \(q_D^s\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}factorization}\), the joint law of the district blocks is their product.  Thus finite recursive evaluation and total probability give, for every declared counterfactual cell \(C\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{M^s}(C)
&=\sum_{\omega\in\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}\Omega_D}
\mathbf 1\{C\text{ is true under recursive evaluation of }\omega\}
\prod_{D\in\mathcal D(G)}q_D^s(\omega_D)\\
&=\Psi_C^s(\theta^s).
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
If \(D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing\), \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}kernel\text{-}invariance}\) gives \(q_D^s=q_D^\star\).  For each complete supplied cell, \(\mathrm{ass:typed\text{-}menu\text{-}realizability}\) and (5) give
\[
\Psi_{C_{a,v}}^s(\theta^s)=P_{M^s}^{a}(v)=P_a^s(v).
\]
Hence \(\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\), proving the left-to-right saturated range inclusion simultaneously for every finite \(\mathcal F\).

Conversely, take \(\theta\in\Theta(\mathcal P)\).  Nonemptiness of every alphabet permits an injective deterministic completion \(\iota_D:\Omega_D\to\Omega_D^{\mathrm{all}}\) at the finitely many unvisited parent configurations.  Push each \(q_D^s\) forward through \(\iota_D\), take the district blocks independently, and let each structural equation read its component response map.  Acyclicity of \(G\) gives unique recursive evaluation, and every output lies in \(\mathcal X\).  The defining clauses of \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat}}\) admit each independent collection of full district-response laws because every district is bidirected complete and every law on its full response block is permitted.  Using the same \(\iota_D\) in every domain turns each equality \(q_D^s=q_D^\star\) for an unchanged district into equality of its completed full-block laws.  The complete-cell equations in \(\Theta(\mathcal P)\) imply
\[
P_{M_\theta^s}^{a}(v)
=\Psi_{C_{a,v}}^s(\theta^s)
=P_a^s(v)
\]
for all \(s,a,v\).  Therefore \(\mathbf M_\theta\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat}}(\mathcal P)\), uses the original alphabets, and realizes every corresponding \(\Psi\)-value.  This proves the reverse saturated range inclusion.

For the arbitrary-ADMG row, take \(\mathbf M\in\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:recursive\text{-}compatibility}\), each \(M^s\) is a finite recursive SCM on \((G,\mathcal X)\).  Apply \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}canonical\text{-}counterfactual\text{-}equivalence}\) in each domain to the finite joint collection containing all response-map counterfactuals visited by the supplied cells and the target cells in \(\mathcal F\).  The resulting graph-compatible canonical model has the same observed alphabets and the same joint counterfactual law.  In particular it preserves each district response-profile law, so \(\mathrm{ass:district\text{-}kernel\text{-}invariance}\) gives
\[
q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^s(\mathord\cdot;\vartheta^s)
=q_{D,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\mathord\cdot;\vartheta^\star)
\quad\text{whenever }D\cap\Delta_s=\varnothing.
\]
Preservation of every complete supplied cell gives
\[
\Phi_{C_{a,v},\mathrm{can}}^s(\vartheta^s)=P_a^s(v).
\]
Thus \(\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\), and preservation of all cells in \(\mathcal F\) proves one canonical range inclusion.

Conversely, a point \(\vartheta\in\Theta_G^{\mathrm{can}}(\mathcal P)\) consists of graph-compatible one-hot structural tables and finite canonical exogenous probability vectors.  The one-hot constraints select one value in \(\mathcal X_V\) for every structural input; the simplex constraints define probability laws; and the graph-compatible latent restrictions and the product law across districts give recursive compatibility and district factorization.  The response-law equalities give district-kernel invariance, while district closure is a fixed condition of the model-class instance.  The equation for every complete supplied cell gives the entire corresponding supplied law.  Hence the canonical realization lies in \(\mathcal C(\mathcal P)\), uses the original alphabets, and has target-cell probabilities \(\Phi_{C,\mathrm{can}}^\star(\vartheta^\star)\).  This proves the reverse canonical inclusion.

Both parameter fibers are finite-dimensional.  The saturated fiber is a closed subset of a finite product of probability simplices cut out by finitely many polynomial equalities.  The graph-compatible canonical fiber is a closed subset of a finite union of products of probability simplices and finite one-hot sets cut out by finitely many polynomial equalities and inequalities.  Both are bounded, hence compact, and are semialgebraic by their displayed finite polynomial descriptions.  Their nonemptiness follows from the assumed nonempty SCM fiber and the corresponding forward inclusion.  In each summand in (5), at most one coordinate occurs from each district block visited by \(C\).  Therefore \(\Psi_C^s\) is multi-affine and has total degree at most the number of visited districts.

Fix either exact range equality and a target cell \(T\).  The target polynomial is continuous on a nonempty compact fiber, so it attains a minimum and maximum.  The range equality makes these respectively the sharp lower and upper bounds over the corresponding SCM fiber, with both endpoints realized on the original alphabets.  Cell probabilities lie in \([0,1]\); hence at least one endpoint is strictly inside the logical interval exactly when the lower endpoint is positive or the upper endpoint is less than one.  The cell is identified exactly when the extrema agree.  If they differ, attaining minimizers and maximizers yield same-menu original-alphabet SCM families with unequal target values.  This proves endpoint sharpness without asserting that intermediate values are attained.

Apply the same compactness argument to the nonnegative evidence polynomial.  If its attained maximum is zero, evidence is zero throughout the fiber.  If its attained minimum is zero and its maximum is positive, a compatible minimizing model has zero evidence, so positivity is not uniform.  In both cases a conditional functional on the entire fiber is rejected before division.  If the evidence minimum is strictly positive, the ratio
\[
x\longmapsto
\frac{\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}
{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}
\]
is continuous on the compact fiber.  It attains its sharp lower and upper conditional bounds, and the exact range equality supplies endpoint SCMs.  Distinct extrema give distinct same-menu original-alphabet models; no interval-filling property is used.

For two arms, the denominator is common.  Under the same strict positivity condition,
\[
Q_\sigma^\star(\mathbf M_x)-Q_\rho^\star(\mathbf M_x)
=\frac{\Xi_{B_\sigma\cap E}^\star(x^\star)
-\Xi_{B_\rho\cap E}^\star(x^\star)}
{\Xi_E^\star(x^\star)}.
\]
The denominator is positive, so the two sides have the sign of the numerator gap.  A continuous numerator-gap polynomial that is positive everywhere on a compact fiber has a strictly positive attained minimum, and the converse is immediate.  A negative minimum and a positive maximum are attained by two same-menu original-alphabet models with opposite strict rankings; conversely, any such pair forces the two strict endpoint inequalities.  This proves the exact pruning test.

Finally, the broad part of \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}district\text{-}fiber\text{-}projection}\) gives
\[
\mathcal Q_D(\mathcal P)\subseteq\mathcal K_D(m_D)
\]
for every \(D\).  Under \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\), its focal part strengthens this to
\[
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{sat},D}(\mathcal P)=\mathcal K_D(m_D).
\]
The proof freezes every nonfocal response law.  For a transport-admissible complete supplied cell \(C\), changing the focal law from \(q_0\) to \(q\) changes its probability by
\[
\sum_{\omega_{-D}}\nu^s(\omega_{-D})
\chi_{C,\omega_{-D}}(q-q_0),
\]
and each summand vanishes because \(\chi_{C,\omega_{-D}}\in R_D(m_D)\) while \(q-q_0\) annihilates \(R_D(m_D)\).  Thus a cross-district indicator is compatible with exact local projection whenever its active slices satisfy this condition; cross-district coupling alone is not an obstruction.  The strictness part of \(\mathrm{lem:structural\text{-}separation\text{-}implies\text{-}active\text{-}slice}\) shows why \(\mathsf{Sep}_D\) is sufficient but not necessary.

This focal statement changes only the full response-block law at \(D\) and its unchanged-source copies, leaving every \(D'\ne D\) at a graph-compatible baseline.  The first exact global row instead uses \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{sat}}\), in which every district is saturated, because its full multi-affine fiber permits simultaneous Cartesian variation of all district laws.  Outside the focal projection theorem's hypotheses, the local face is certified only as an outer relaxation, so failed local membership is not a global nonidentification certificate.  Whenever the extrema of the appropriate exact global program differ, the proved exact range equality supplies the required pair of original-alphabet same-menu SCMs.

statements.statement:
For every district \(D\),
\[
\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\Longrightarrow\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P).
\]
The implication is strict in general.  In particular, take two independent binary response coordinates \(Y_0\) and \(Z\) generated by distinct singleton districts, let \(D\) be the district generating \(Y_0\), and supply in the target domain both the complete marginal law of \(Y_0\) and the complete joint law of \((Y_0,Z)\).  The resulting menu satisfies \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) but not \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\).
statements.proof_tex:
Assume \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\), and fix a transport-admissible complete supplied cell \(C\) and a nonfocal profile \(\omega_{-D}\).  By \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}separated\text{-}menu}\), at least one of the two permitted structural cases applies.  If the recursive indicator of \(C\) is independent of \(\omega_D\), then its fixed-\(\omega_{-D}\) slice is either the zero row or \(\mathbf 1^\top\).  The zero row belongs to every row space, and \(\mathbf 1^\top\in\operatorname{row}(A_D)\) because \(\mathrm{def:stacked\text{-}menu\text{-}system}\) prepends the normalization row.  Hence the slice lies in \(R_D(m_D)\).

If instead the indicator depends only on \(\omega_D\), \(\mathrm{def:district\text{-}separated\text{-}menu}\) requires its raw row to occur in \(A_D\).  Every fixed-\(\omega_{-D}\) slice is that raw row, so it belongs to \(\operatorname{row}(A_D)\subseteq R_D(m_D)\).  These cases cover every admissible cell and every nonfocal profile, proving \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\).

For strictness, consider two binary response coordinates \(Y_0\) and \(Z\) generated by independent singleton district blocks, and put \(D=D_{Y_0}\).  For \(y,z\in\{0,1\}\), define
\[
h_y(\omega_D)=\mathbf 1\{Y_0(\omega_D)=y\},
\qquad
k_z(\omega_{-D})=\mathbf 1\{Z(\omega_{-D})=z\}.
\]
Supplying the complete marginal law of \(Y_0\) retains both rows \(h_0,h_1\) in \(A_D\).  The complete joint cell \(\{Y_0=y,Z=z\}\) has the genuine cross-district indicator
\[
h_y(\omega_D)k_z(\omega_{-D}).
\]
Because the binary profile sets contain profiles producing both values, this indicator is neither independent of \(\omega_D\) nor a function of \(\omega_D\) alone.  Thus \(\mathsf{Sep}_D(\mathcal P)\) fails.  On fixing \(\omega_{-D}\), however, its focal slice is \(0\) when \(k_z(\omega_{-D})=0\) and is \(h_y\) when \(k_z(\omega_{-D})=1\).  Both rows belong to \(\operatorname{row}(A_D)\).  The marginal cells have slices \(h_y\), and the same argument applies to every joint cell.  Therefore every required slice belongs to \(R_D(m_D)\), so \(\mathsf{ASep}_D(\mathcal P)\) holds.  Independent Bernoulli laws on the two finite singleton response blocks realize the supplied marginal and joint laws on the declared binary alphabets, completing the promised strict example.

tldr: Heterogeneous sites can supply genuine Layer-3 partial-copy laws. A certified extraction judgment turns each available context and cell into a typed district row only after source admissibility is proved. On a fixed-alphabet one-district compatibility face, the sharp transported arm-gap equals an explicit dual weighting of all retained source-labelled cells, and an added Layer-3 regime block yields a finite piecewise-affine pruning frontier. DCTFTR is an inductive, terminating transition system with typed failures and zero-evidence rejection. A complete binary instance gives the margin \(2p-1/2\), while minimum-cost regime-block acquisition and multi-district face preservation remain explicit open questions.

project_justification.gap: CTFTR transports conditional counterfactuals from heterogeneous Layer-1/2 inputs, CTFIDU+ identifies from Layer-3 inputs in one causal specification, and Park--Lee pruning uses graph-based action classes or fixed transported bounds. None derives an exact source-menu certificate or a sign-regime boundary for the order of conditional Layer-3 arms.
project_justification.niche: District-closed shifts and common-evidence arm comparisons reduce one confounded target block to a boundary-sensitive response polytope. Its LP dual converts released source cells into an auditable ranking certificate, while a candidate menu value parametrizes a genuine pruning phase transition.
project_justification.fill: The project proves fixed-alphabet realization of the compatible face, gives certified typed extraction and an inductive DCTFTR semantics, replaces global row span by an active-face criterion, derives sharp primal--dual arm-order certificates, verifies the complete binary phase boundary, and poses minimum-cost regime-block acquisition before asking whether the construction survives multi-district gluing.

related_work: Correa, Lee, and Bareinboim (2022, Theorem 5.1) supply the source-labelled conditional transport architecture for Layers 1 and 2; Proposition 1 proves proper typed inclusion of their problem-instance subgrammar and sound semantic agreement of successful functionals, without asserting syntactic or transition-level equivalence. Raghavan and Bareinboim (2026, Theorem 3.5 and Appendix E.1) supply Layer-3 factor extraction and ctf-thickets for one causal specification; Proposition 1 embeds that setting through \(\mathcal S=\{\star\}\) and proves non-representability of the complete binary multi-domain instance, without claiming that its scalar cell alone is outside CTFIDU+. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022, Theorem 2.4) supply the finite response carrier, and Choe et al. (2026, Proposition 3.1) motivate preserving all information rows; both inform rather than serve as tightening targets. Bareinboim and Pearl (2012, Theorems 5--7) and Bareinboim and Pearl (2014) supply vertex-level selection diagrams and multi-environment completeness, whereas district joint-kernel invariance is a stronger Layer-3 transport condition. Park and Lee (2026, ICLR, Theorems 1--3) define realizable Layer-3 action classes, and Park and Lee (2026, UAI, Theorems 1--2) give valid Layer-1/2 transported bandit bounds; they inform the menu-dual order certificate, binary pruning boundary, and ex-post block-acquisition question rather than serving as results claimed to be beaten.
technical_internal_limitation: Boundary fibers require the active normals \(e_\omega\) for \(\omega\in Z_D(m_D)\); ordinary row span alone can miss identification when the menu forces response profiles to zero. Multi-district completeness is not asserted. The smallest binary two-hedge thicket must compare every recursive failure with target-score constancy on the exact global compatibility fiber; a failed recursion with a constant target would redirect the global claim to sharp polynomial transported bounds.
honest_scope: The face projection, active-face identification criterion, dual arm-order theorem, one-cell phase diagram, and complete binary check concern a reduced one-district comparison with common positive evidence. DCTFTR soundness covers broader district-closed instances, but fixed-cardinality multi-district completeness is open. The acquisition objective is finite and ex post; it is not an ex-ante adaptive policy. No assumption supplies the dominance margin, active face, or threshold. The observational and hard-interventional problem-instance subgrammar is properly included in DCTFTR and successful outputs agree semantically with the target, the one-domain problem-instance class includes the CTFIDU+ setting, and sure evidence reduces conditional arm order to the unconditional numerator-gap program.
